'''Christy Lynn Haynes''' (born July 31, 1977) is a chemist at the [[University of Minnesota]]. She works at the interface of [[Analytical chemistry|analytical]], [[Chemical biology|biological]], and [[nanomaterials]] chemistry.

== Early life and education ==
Haynes was born in [[Scottsdale, Arizona]], in 1977.<ref name="cv">{{cite web|title=CV: Christy Lynn Haynes|url=http://www1.chem.umn.edu/groups/haynes/docs/cv_01062016.pdf|access-date=13 May 2018}}</ref> She completed her undergraduate work at [[Macalester College]], in 1998 with a major in chemistry and minors in mathematics and Spanish. She completed her postbaccalaureate work at [[Northwestern University]] completing a master's degree in 1999 and a Ph.D. in 2003 under the direction of Richard P. Van Duyne. Her dissertation, "Fundamentals and Applications of Nanoparticle Optics and Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering," demonstrated how [[Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy]] could be used as a small molecule biosensor.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Fundamentals and applications of nanoparticle optics and surface-enhanced Raman scattering|last=Lynn.|first=Haynes, Christy|date=2003|isbn=978-0496356829|oclc=271306389}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Haynes|first1=Christy L.|last2=McFarland|first2=Adam D.|last3=Duyne|first3=Richard P. Van|date=September 2005|title=Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy|journal=Analytical Chemistry|volume=77|issue=17|pages=338 A–346 A|doi=10.1021/ac053456d|issn=0003-2700|doi-access=free}}</ref> She was awarded the [[Northwestern University]] prize for Excellence in Graduate Research in 2002.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://chem.umn.edu/profiles/christy-haynes|title=Christy Haynes|last=harva015|date=2016-06-06|work=Department of Chemistry|access-date=2018-05-11}}</ref>  Haynes completed post-doctoral work at [[University of North Carolina Chapel Hill]] in 2005 in the lab of [[Mark Wightman|R. Mark Wightman]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=2016-06-06|title=Chrisy L. Haynes|url=https://chem.umn.edu/profiles/christy-haynes|access-date=2019-03-07|website=University of Minnesota}}</ref> She has described [[Hilary Godwin]], then professor at [[Northwestern University]], as one of her influences.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://blavatnikawards.org/news/items/here-are-women-shaping-future-science/|title=Here Are the Women Shaping the Future of Science {{!}} Blavatnik Awards for Young Scientists|website=blavatnikawards.org|access-date=2020-01-19}}</ref>

== Career ==
After her PhD, Haynes worked with [[Mark Wightman]] as a postdoctoral fellow at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://oxide.jhu.edu/2/board/haynes|title=Prof. Christy Haynes {{!}} OXIDE|website=oxide.jhu.edu|access-date=2018-05-12}}</ref> There she worked on [[microelectrode]] [[amperometry]] to study single-cell exocytosis.<ref name=":2" />

Haynes joined the [[University of Minnesota]] in 2005 as an assistant professor.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.peoplebehindthescience.com/dr-christy-haynes/|title=391: Dr. Christy Haynes: Tiny Technology with Big Impacts: Nanoparticles for Medicine, Energy, and the Environment – People Behind the Science Podcast|website=www.peoplebehindthescience.com|access-date=2018-05-11|date=2017-04-03}}</ref> She was promoted to full professor in 2014 and became the Elmore H. Northey Professor of Chemistry in 2015. Haynes has been the associate head of department of chemistry since 2015.<ref name=":3" /> She became a Distinguished McKnight University Professor in 2019.<ref name="cv" />

In 2012, Haynes helped establish the Center for Sustainable Nanotechnology, which researches the transformations and interactions of consumer or industrial nanomaterials in the environment.<ref>{{Cite web|title=About Us {{!}} The Center for Sustainable Nanotechnology|url=https://susnano.wisc.edu/about/|access-date=2021-01-26|language=en-US}}</ref> Since 2012, Haynes has been the associate director of the Center for Sustainable Nanotechnology. As part of this effort, Haynes helps author the blog Sustainable Nano, where she has contributed posts on diversity in the sciences and science communication.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Christy Haynes|url=https://sustainable-nano.com/author/clh731/|access-date=2021-05-20|website=Sustainable Nano|language=en}}</ref>

In 2017 she delivered a [[TED talk]], "Nanomaterials are everywhere; how do we make them safe?".<ref>{{Citation|last=TEDx Talks|title=Nanomaterials are everywhere; how do we make them safe? {{!}} Christy L. Haynes {{!}} TEDxEdina|date=2017-05-05|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FRP0lGEOQPE|access-date=2018-05-11}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=TEDxEdina {{!}} TED|url=https://www.ted.com/tedx/events/20626|access-date=2018-05-12|website=www.ted.com}}</ref> Haynes was named in The Analytical Scientist Power List in 2016, 2017, and 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The Power List 2019|url=https://theanalyticalscientist.com/powerlist/2019|access-date=2020-03-05|work=The Analytical Scientist|archive-date=2023-03-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230306205231/https://theanalyticalscientist.com/powerlist/2019|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2017, 2018, and 2019, Haynes was named a finalist for the [[Blavatnik Awards for Young Scientists|Blavatnik National Awards for Young Scientists]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=National Finalists {{!}} Blavatnik Awards for Young Scientists|url=http://blavatnikawards.org/honorees/national-finalists/|access-date=2021-05-20|website=blavatnikawards.org}}</ref> In 2018, she was awarded a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]], which enabled her to work in the [[Technical University of Valencia]] characterizing nanomaterials in an environmental matrix.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Northwestern chemist receives 2018 Guggenheim Fellowship – Northwestern Now|url=https://news.northwestern.edu/stories/2018/april/northwestern-chemist-receives-2018-guggenheim-fellowship/|access-date=2018-05-11|website=news.northwestern.edu}}</ref><ref name=":1" /> She delivered a second [[TED talk]] in 2022 entitled "How nanoparticles can help solve the global food crisis".<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KMoLHXfa8l4 | title=How nanoparticles can help solve the global food crisis &#124; Christy Haynes &#124; TEDxMinneapolis | website=[[YouTube]] | date=9 December 2022 }}</ref>

Haynes is an advocate for increased diversity in the chemical sciences.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Professor Christy Haynes {{!}} The Center for Sustainable Nanotechnology|url=https://susnano.wisc.edu/our-team-members/christy-haynes/|access-date=2018-05-11|website=susnano.wisc.edu |date=23 December 2014 }}</ref> She takes part in outreach activities to encourage young people to consider careers in chemistry.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Christy Haynes {{!}} FabFems|url=https://www.fabfems.org/users/christy-haynes|access-date=2018-05-12|website=www.fabfems.org}}</ref> She is a lead presenter for the [[University of Minnesota]] ''Energy and U'' program, which brings over ten thousand third grade students to her campus each year.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|title=Chemistry Professor Christy Haynes awarded prestigious Guggenheim Fellowship – College of Science and Engineering|work=College of Science and Engineering|url=https://cse.umn.edu/news-release/chemistry-professor-christy-haynes-awarded-prestigious-guggenheim-fellowship/|url-status=dead|access-date=2018-05-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180512044140/https://cse.umn.edu/news-release/chemistry-professor-christy-haynes-awarded-prestigious-guggenheim-fellowship/|archive-date=2018-05-12}}</ref> Haynes is a member of the advisory board for Open Chemical Collaborative in Diversity Equity (OXIDE).<ref>{{Cite web|title=OXIDE Advisory Board {{!}} OXIDE|url=http://oxide.jhu.edu/2/board|access-date=2021-05-20|website=oxide.jhu.edu}}</ref>

Haynes is passionate about her role as a mentor and advisor to students—telling Northwestern University in an alumni spotlight in 2020, <blockquote>"Professionally, my CV does not really reveal the great pride and honor I feel to work with the undergraduate and graduate students who join my laboratory or collaborate with my group. Each of those students has a story about how they arrived in chemistry, the challenges they’ve overcome, and the skills that they are currently working on to become even better. I love learning these stories and being a part of them."<ref>{{Cite web|title=Alumna Spotlight: Christy L. Haynes: Department of Chemistry – Northwestern University|url=https://chemistry.northwestern.edu/about/newsletter/2020-newsletters/spring-2020-newsletter/alumna-spotlight-christy.html|access-date=2021-05-20|website=chemistry.northwestern.edu|language=en}}</ref></blockquote>Haynes has been recognized for her mentoring and advising efforts. The University of Minnesota Graduate and Professional Student Assembly awarded her the Advising and Mentoring Award in 2015 and the University of Minnesota gave her the 2013 Outstanding Postdoctoral Mentor Award.<ref name="cv" />

== Research ==
Her lab, the Haynes Research Group, applies analytical chemistry and nanomaterials to biomedicine, ecology and toxicology.<ref name=":3" /> Nanoparticles are increasingly being used in manufacturing, which will result in them ending up in the ecosystem with unknown consequences.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Haynes|first=Christy L.|date=2010-09-01|title=The emerging field of nanotoxicology|journal=Analytical and Bioanalytical Chemistry|volume=398|issue=2|pages=587–588|doi=10.1007/s00216-010-3972-5|issn=1618-2642|pmid=20652553|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite web|title=Design and Redesign of Sustainable Engineered Nanomaterials: Christy Haynes (University of Minnesota) {{!}} U-M LSA Chemistry|url=https://lsa.umich.edu/chem/news-events/all-events.detail.html/40779-8750075.html|access-date=2018-05-12|website=lsa.umich.edu}}</ref> The Haynes group look to determine the molecular design rules for nanoparticle toxicity, through material design and fabrication and characterization both in the lab and in the food web.<ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Events Calendar – Department of Chemistry – The University of Utah|url=https://chem.utah.edu/events/index.php?trumbaEmbed=view=event&eventid=123644467|access-date=2018-05-12|website=chem.utah.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=2013-04-18|title=Sizing Up Nanotechnology Safety|work=EHS Today|url=http://www.ehstoday.com/safety/sizing-nanotechnology-safety|access-date=2018-05-12}}</ref> They characterize chemical messenger synthesis and exocytosis using laser spectroscopy and microelectrochemistry.<ref name=":2" /> In 2012, her group was the first ever to successfully measure real-time chemical messenger delivery from individual blood platelets.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Brilliant 10: Christy Haynes Reveals the Secrets of the Body's Blood-Clotting System|work=Popular Science|url=https://www.popsci.com/science/article/2012-09/christy-haynes-reveals-secrets-bodys-blood-clotting-system|access-date=2018-05-12}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Weber|first=Tom|title=Univ. of Minn. chemist seeks greater understanding of blood|url=https://www.mprnews.org/story/2013/02/18/daily-circuit-field-notes|access-date=2018-05-12}}</ref> In 2013, her research was discussed on [[Minnesota Public Radio]].<ref>{{Cite news|last=Weber|first=Tom|title=Univ. of Minn. chemist seeks greater understanding of blood|url=http://minnesota.publicradio.org/display/web/2013/02/18/daily-circuit-field-notes|access-date=2018-05-11}}</ref>

=== Publications and journal contributions ===

==== As author ====
Haynes has published over 200 peer-reviewed articles in scientific journals.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Publications|url=http://www1.chem.umn.edu/groups/haynes/publications.html|access-date=2020-03-05|work=Haynes Research Group}}</ref>

==== As editor ====
Since 2016, she has served as an associate editor of academic journal ''Analytical Chemistry'', and in 2018 became the curator of feature articles and perspectives for the journal.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Analytical Chemistry|url=https://pubs.acs.org/page/ancham/editors.html|access-date=2021-05-20|website=pubs.acs.org|language=en}}</ref> She was on the editorial board of [[Analytical Chemistry (journal)|''Analytical Chemistry'']] from 2013 to 2016 prior to becoming an editor. Haynes was the vice editor in chief of the journal ''Environmental Science: Nano'' from 2013 to 2015.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|title=Environmental Science: Nano journal|url=https://www.rsc.org/journals-books-databases/about-journals/environmental-science-nano/|access-date=2021-05-20|website=Royal Society of Chemistry|language=en-GB}}</ref> She currently sits on the editorial advisory boards of a number of academic journals, including ''[[Journal of Raman Spectroscopy]]'' since 2009,<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://analyticalsciencejournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/hub/journal/10974555/homepage/editorialboard.html|title=Journal of Raman Spectroscopy|publisher=Wiley|language=en|doi=10.1002/(ISSN)1097-4555}}</ref> [[Chemical Science (journal)|''Chemical Science'']] since 2010,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chemical Science journal|url=https://www.rsc.org/journals-books-databases/about-journals/chemical-science/|access-date=2021-05-20|website=Royal Society of Chemistry|date=22 May 2015 |language=en-GB}}</ref> ''The Analyst'' since 2010,<ref name="cv" /> ''[[Chemical Research in Toxicology]]'' since 2013,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Editorial Board|url=https://pubs.acs.org/page/crtoec/editors.html|access-date=2021-05-20|website=pubs.acs.org|language=en}}</ref> [[Royal Society of Chemistry|''Environmental Science: Nano'']] since 2016,<ref name=":5" /> ''[[ACS Nano]]'' since 2020,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Editorial Board|url=https://pubs.acs.org/page/ancac3/editors.html|access-date=2021-05-20|website=pubs.acs.org|language=en}}</ref> and ''Nanoscale and Nanoscale Advances'' since 2020<ref>{{Cite web|title=Nanoscale Advances|url=https://www.rsc.org/journals-books-databases/about-journals/nanoscale-advances/|access-date=2021-05-20|website=Royal Society of Chemistry|language=en-GB}}</ref>
